blocks.html: Linear regression (recall Chapter 12) models a continuous outcome whose errors are roughly Normal. Many outcomes in Community Medicine are not like that: a household joins CBHI or it does not, a village records so many malaria cases. This chapter shows that linear regression is one member of a larger family, the generalised linear models, and builds the members you will use most: logistic regression for binary outcomes and its variants (§13.2–13.3), Poisson and negative binomial regression for counts and rates (§13.4–13.6), and models that estimate prevalence and risk ratios directly (§13.7).
